cards.f: Why do typhoid ulcers run parallel to bowel?
cards.b: Ulcers form in Peyer's patches naturally arranged longitudinally along ileum. Necrosis/slough maintains this longitudinal orientation
Salmonella typhi or Salmonella paratyphi causing enteric fever

cards.f: Why perforation occurs in typhoid ulcers?
cards.b: Typhoid ulcers acute without significant fibrosis/chronic inflammation. When necrotic slough separates, bowel wall weakened, highly susceptible to perforation
flask-shaped with narrow neck and broad base, located in large intestine (cecum, sigmoid, rectum). Intervening mucosa normal
Flask-shaped - narrow neck at mucosal surface where parasite enters, widening with liquefactive necrosis in submucosa
Entamoeba histolytica. Trophozoites cause liquefactive necrosis and erythrophagocytosis (engulfing RBCs)
Localized hyperplastic mass of granulation tissue/fibrosis in bowel wall from chronic amoebic infection, mimics colon cancer
Perforation → peritonitis, hemorrhage, stricture formation, amoeboma, amoebic liver abscess
Turkish towel appearance - multiple small necrotic blackish areas with pinpoint ulcers on hyperemic/edematous mucosa

cards.f: Turkish towel appearance in bacillary colitis?
cards.b: Mucosa hyperemic/edematous with multiple pinpoint ulcers giving rough, velvety appearance like Turkish towel
Shigella dysenteriae
Bacillary - superficial ulcers, Turkish towel, Shigella. Amoebic - flask-shaped deep ulcers, Entamoeba, normal intervening mucosa
transversely to bowel long axis with undermined margins. Lead to stricture formation from fibrosis

cards.f: Why TB ulcers lead to stricture formation?
cards.b: Transverse orientation across bowel. As ulcer heals with significant fibrosis/contraction, narrows bowel circumference → stricture
Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Primary from M. bovis in infected milk; secondary from self-swallowing sputum in active pulmonary TB

cards.f: Differentiate TB from typhoid ulcers by orientation?
cards.b: TB ulcers transverse (follow lymphatic channels). Typhoid ulcers longitudinal (follow Peyer's patches arrangement)
most common neoplastic colon polyp. May be sessile/pedunculated. Malignant transformation risk increases with size >2 cm and villous component

cards.f: Malignant transformation risk in tubular adenomas?
cards.b: Depends on size (>2 cm), villous component, degree of dysplasia. Increased risk with larger size and villous features
ulcerative (left-sided, napkin ring constriction) and fungating (right-sided, polypoid mass). Ulcerative affects descending/sigmoid. Fungating affects cecum/ascending

cards.f: Napkin ring appearance in colon cancer?
cards.b: Ulcerative tumour constricting bowel lumen circumferentially, giving annular narrowing resembling napkin ring - left-sided colon cancers
Low fiber diet (low stool bulk), FAP (inherited), Lynch syndrome (HNPCC)
solitary ulcer with punched-out edges, margins continuous with surrounding mucosa, converging rugae

cards.f: Four histological layers of chronic peptic ulcer?
cards.b: From surface inward: necrotic layer, inflammatory exudate, granulation tissue, fibrous scar

cards.f: Most common cause of chronic peptic ulcer?
cards.b: H. pylori infection. Others: NSAIDs, alcohol, tobacco, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome

cards.f: Differentiate benign from malignant ulcer on gross exam?
cards.b: Benign - punched-out edges, flat margins continuous with mucosa. Malignant - rolled, everted, heaped-up edges, irregular, dirty base
Obstruction (hourglass), hemorrhage (coffee ground vomitus), perforation (air under diaphragm), malignant transformation (<1% gastric ulcers)
small hole on serosal surface (≈0.5 cm), full-thickness defect through all layers. Rugae near ulcer flattened

cards.f: Characteristic radiological sign of perforated peptic ulcer?
cards.b: Pneumoperitoneum - free air under diaphragm, visible below right hemidiaphragm on erect chest/abdominal X-ray
leather bottle appearance - stomach wall thickened from extensive desmoplasia. Classic histology is signet ring cell carcinoma
Metastatic carcinoma in ovaries, typically from stomach, characterized by bilateral involvement and signet ring cells
direct to peritoneum/ovaries (Krukenberg), lymphatic to Virchow's node (Troisier's sign), hematogenous to liver/lungs/brain

cards.f: Esophageal carcinoma has three gross patterns:
cards.b: polypoid fungating (most common), ulcerative, diffuse infiltrative (annular stenosing)

cards.f: Differentiate two main esophageal carcinoma types by location/etiology?
cards.b: SCC - upper/middle third, strongly associated with smoking, alcohol, nutritional deficiencies. Adenocarcinoma - lower third, chronic GERD → Barrett's
Tracheoesophageal fistula, progressive dysphagia, weight loss, hemorrhage
sequestrum (dead bone) surrounded by involucrum (reactive new bone). Most common cause is Staphylococcus aureus
Piece of dead bone separated from surrounding healthy bone during necrosis in osteomyelitis, acts as foreign body perpetuating infection
Sheath of reactive new bone formed by periosteum surrounding sequestrum/infected area, represents body's attempt to wall off infection
Septicemia, pathologic fractures, squamous cell carcinoma in long-standing sinus tracts (Marjolin's ulcer), secondary amyloidosis

cards.f: Giant cell tumour of bone (osteoclastoma) shows
cards.b: soap bubble appearance on X-ray. Cut surface shows multiple cystic areas with blood clots and honey comb septal appearance

cards.f: Which cells are neoplastic in giant cell tumour of bone?
cards.b: Mononuclear stromal cells - giant cells are reactive osteoclasts recruited by tumour
Codman's triangle and sun ray appearance on X-ray. Arises from metaphysis of long bones. Defining feature is malignant cells directly producing osteoid
Direct production of irregular, lace-like osteoid (immature bone matrix) by malignant cells
punched-out lytic lesions with no sclerotic rim. Malignant cells are monoclonal plasma cells with clock-face chromatin
Hypercalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, Bone abnormalities (lytic lesions) - hallmark clinical features for symptomatic myeloma diagnosis
Hypercalcemia, renal failure (cast nephropathy), anemia, pathologic fractures
yellowish-white fatty deposits on intimal surface. Ulcerated plaques show porridge-like necrotic core. Distribution around arterial ostia

cards.f: Porridge-like material in atheromatous plaque center?
cards.b: Mixture of necrotic cellular debris, extracellular lipids (cholesterol), calcium salts from foam cell death and extracellular matrix breakdown
IHD/MI, gangrene of extremities, stroke, aneurysm, thrombosis/embolism
hard white calcified patches, intima cracks like shell when opened. This is dystrophic calcification (normal serum calcium)

cards.f: Calcification type in atherosclerosis and difference from metastatic?
cards.b: Dystrophic - in dead/dying tissue despite normal serum calcium. Metastatic - in normal tissue from hypercalcemia
extreme dilation of aortic diameter (>50% increase) with wall thinning. Most common AAA cause is severe atherosclerosis

cards.f: Most common cause of abdominal aortic aneurysms?
cards.b: Severe atherosclerosis - atheromatous plaques impair oxygen diffusion to media, causing atrophy and wall weakening
rough, shaggy pericardium with yellowish-white fibrin strands. Layers separated give bread and butter appearance
Myocardial infarction (Dressler's or acute phase), uremia, rheumatic heart disease, radiation, lupus
tree-bark appearance of intima - greyish-white firm fibrous plaques with wrinkled intervening intima. Caused by Treponema pallidum in tertiary syphilis

cards.f: Why intima looks like tree bark in syphilitic aortitis?
cards.b: Chronic inflammation destroys elastic fibres in media; intima collapses/wrinkles over scarred, retracted media creating tree-bark appearance
pale, yellowish-white soft areas in myocardium (not fibrosed). No grey-white scar indicates recent, not healed

cards.f: What is contraction band in MI?
cards.b: Intensely eosinophilic transverse bands in myocytes from hypercontraction of sarcomeres when calcium rushes into cell after reperfusion
shrunken, thin, grey-white hard fibrous scar. Takes approximately 2-3 months for full scar formation
Lines of Zahn - alternating pale (platelets/fibrin) and dark (RBC) layers, indicating formation in flowing blood (antemortem)
Thrombus - dry, friable, adherent to vessel wall, Lines of Zahn. Postmortem clot - gelatinous, elastic, not adherent, chicken fat/currant jelly appearance
small warty vegetations (verrucae) arranged in single row along valve closure lines. Affects mitral and aortic valves
Microscopic granulomatous lesions in myocardium, pathognomonic for Rheumatic Heart Disease, containing Anitschkow cells (macrophages with wavy chromatin)
thickened LV wall (>1.5 cm), narrowed LV lumen (concentric), IV septum shifted to right. Most common cause is systemic hypertension

cards.f: Difference between concentric and eccentric hypertrophy?
cards.b: Concentric - thickens wall without dilating lumen (pressure overload: hypertension, aortic stenosis). Eccentric - dilates lumen with proportional wall thickening (volume overload)
fish mouth or buttonhole appearance - thickened, fibrosed leaflets with fused commissures. Most common cause is Rheumatic Heart Disease

cards.f: Why mitral stenosis causes pulmonary brown induration?
cards.b: Back pressure into left atrium/pulmonary veins causes chronic congestion; RBCs leak into alveoli where macrophages phagocytose and accumulate hemosiderin, turning lungs brown/firm
Angina, Syncope, Dyspnea (ASD). Auscultation reveals harsh systolic ejection murmur radiating to carotids

cards.f: Differentiate rheumatic from senile calcific aortic stenosis?
cards.b: Rheumatic - almost always with mitral disease, fused commissures. Senile calcific - elderly, only aortic, independently calcified (unfused) leaflets
large, bulky, friable vegetations on both sides of valve cusps. Causes destruction/necrosis of underlying valve tissue

cards.f: What are Osler's nodes and Janeway lesions?
cards.b: Osler's nodes - painful red raised lesions on hands/feet from immune complex deposition. Janeway lesions - painless erythematous macules on palms/soles from septic microemboli
well-circumscribed, encapsulated mass with slit-like pores (compressed ducts). Biphasic tumour of glandular and stromal elements
Well-encapsulated, discrete mass highly mobile, easily moved under skin by patient/examiner
greyish-white hard mass with chalky streaks (desmoplasia). Not well circumscribed - infiltrative margins radiating into fat. Peau d'orange and nipple retraction indicate advanced

cards.f: Causes orange peel (peau d'orange) appearance in breast carcinoma?
cards.b: Obstruction of dermal lymphatic channels by tumour cells causes skin edema, while hair follicles remain tethered down, creating pitted appearance
asymmetric enlargement with multiple nodules separated by fibrous tissue. May show hemorrhage, cystic degeneration, calcification

cards.f: Differentiate Multinodular Goitre from Hashimoto's thyroiditis grossly?
cards.b: MNG - asymmetrical multiple discrete nodules/hemorrhage. Hashimoto's - symmetrical, firm, fleshy, no discrete nodules
symmetrical enlargement, smooth fleshy surface, diffuse fibrosis confined within capsule. Microscopy shows lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centres and Hürthle cells
Hashimoto's - fibrosis confined within thyroid capsule. Riedel's - fibrosis invasive, extends beyond capsule, fixes thyroid to surrounding structures
solitary, encapsulated nodule that compresses surrounding parenchyma without invading. Indistinguishable from follicular carcinoma without capsular/vascular invasion
unilocular cyst lined by skin. Contains hair, sebaceous material, teeth. Has Rokitansky's protuberance with tissues from all three germ layers
Solid nodular projection into dermoid cyst cavity where tissues from all three germ layers concentrated (hair, teeth, bone, cartilage)
multiple well-circumscribed firm nodules with whorled, interlacing grey-white pattern. Most common in premenopausal women from estrogen stimulation
Leiomyoma - multiple, well-circumscribed, firm, whorled cut surface. Leiomyosarcoma - typically single, large, soft, fleshy, ill-defined margins, hemorrhage/necrosis
squamocolumnar junction. Caused by HPV types 16 and 18. Shows fungating, ulcerating, or infiltrative patterns

cards.f: Most common cause renal failure in advanced cervical carcinoma?
cards.b: Tumour infiltration of parametrium compressing/obstructing ureters → bilateral hydronephrosis → renal failure
multilocular cystic mass with solid areas and papillary projections. Serous type associated with BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations

cards.f: What are Psammoma bodies and where common?
cards.b: Concentric, laminated calcifications. Seen in Serous Cystadenocarcinoma ovary, Papillary Carcinoma Thyroid, Meningioma

cards.f: Squamous cell carcinoma of penis shows
cards.b: cauliflower-like fungating growth near glans. Risk factors include HPV, lack of circumcision (smegma accumulation), chronic balanitis

cards.f: How circumcision protects against penile carcinoma?
cards.b: Removes foreskin preventing smegma accumulation - chronic irritant causing chronic inflammation (balanitis), predisposing factor for carcinoma
homogenous, grey-white, lobulated mass. Testis contour retained (doesn't invade tunica). Classic fried-egg cells with lymphocyte-infiltrated fibrous septa
Sheets/lobules of uniform large polygonal cells with clear cytoplasm and central prominent nucleoli (fried egg appearance), separated by fibrous septa with lymphocytes
variegated appearance - grey-white solid, cystic/honey-combed spaces, foci of cartilage/bone. In post-pubertal males, malignant

cards.f: Testicular teratoma behavior differs from ovarian?
cards.b: Ovarian (dermoid) - almost benign. Testicular in post-pubertal males - malignant, metastasises even with well-differentiated tissues
nodular prostate enlargement, spongy cut surface, compressed urethra (slit-like). Bladder shows trabeculation (smooth muscle hypertrophy)

cards.f: Where BPH arises in prostate and differs from cancer?
cards.b: BPH - transition zone surrounding urethra, causes urinary symptoms. Prostate cancer - peripheral zone, palpable DRE but asymptomatic urination until late
pinpoint waxy nodules resembling sago grains. Amyloid deposits in white pulp. Congo Red stain shows apple-green birefringence under polarized light

cards.f: Difference Sago vs Lardaceous Spleen in amyloidosis?
cards.b: Sago - amyloid deposits focally in white pulp, pinpoint granular. Lardaceous - amyloid deposits diffusely in red pulp, large map-like bacon fat appearance
wedge-shaped pale area - base at capsule, apex towards hilum. Pale because spleen has end-arterial blood supply
Referred pain in left shoulder from diaphragmatic irritation (e.g., splenic infarct/rupture), mediated by phrenic nerve
matted lymph nodes with yellowish-white cheese-like necrosis. Caused by tuberculosis (most common). Microscopy shows caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells

cards.f: What is caseous necrosis and where classically seen?
cards.b: Cell death where tissue maintains cheeselike appearance, classically TB; underlying tissue architecture completely obliterated
Potassium ferrocyanide + ferric iron to form blue-colored ferric ferrocyanide - detects hemosiderin deposition
obliteration of sulci/flattening of gyri (cerebral edema), thickened opaque leptomeninges, dense yellowish-white purulent exudate over convexities/base

cards.f: Classic triad acute bacterial meningitis symptoms?
cards.b: Fever, severe headache, neck stiffness (nuchal rigidity)
thickened leptomeninges at base, whitish nodules (tubercles) along Circle of Willis, gelatinous exudate obscuring cranial nerves
Small caseous TB lesion in brain parenchyma/meninges during initial hematogenous spread; TB meningitis occurs when it ruptures into subarachnoid space
multiple well-circumscribed nodules with central caseous necrosis, lacking true capsule. May show calcification
nodular capsulated mass with whorled/trabecular appearance. Compresses brain but doesn't invade. Most common in adult females. Common sites: parasagittal, lateral convexity, wing of sphenoid
Whorls of meningothelial cells with psammoma bodies; uniform nuclei; no mitoses/necrosis (benign)
non-circumscribed, infiltrating mass with irregular margins, necrosis/hemorrhage, ventricle compression. High-grade gliomas show pseudopalisading necrosis
Tumour cells arranged around necrosis areas in palisading pattern - characteristic of glioblastoma multiforme (grade IV)
dark mass of clotted blood with sharply defined borders, narrow necrotic parenchyma rim. Most common cause is hypertension (Charcot-Bouchard aneurysm rupture)
Tiny blister-like aneurysms in small penetrating brain arteries (lenticulostriate) from chronic hypertension; rupture is most common hypertensive hemorrhage cause
liquefactive necrosis. Anaemic infarct is pale/soft with blurred grey-white junction. Hemorrhagic infarct is red, resembling hematoma but soft/necrotic
mildly enlarged kidney with pale smooth subcapsular surface, absent corticomedullary differentiation. Caused by reversible cell injury (mitochondrial swelling)
Calcium (rough, red-brown), Struvite (yellow-white, staghorn), Uric acid (smooth, yellow, laminated), Cystine (smooth, yellow, waxy)
Large branching stone filling renal pelvis/calyces - often struvite, associated with urea-splitting organisms
pale, waxy, translucent kidney. First enlarged then contracted (shrunken). Congo Red shows apple-green birefringence under polarized light
wedge-shaped pale area with apex towards medulla, base under capsule. Narrow preserved rim under capsule (from capsular vessels)
pinpoint whitish lesions surrounded by congestion zone. Caused by septic emboli
diffuse petechial hemorrhages. Seen in malignant nephrosclerosis (onion skin lesions), PSGN, RPGN, HUS, TTP, Goodpasture

cards.f: Onion skin lesion in malignant nephrosclerosis?
cards.b: Concentric arteriolar wall thickening with laminated appearance - characteristic of malignant hypertension
small/shrunken kidney with adherent capsule, finely granular surface, thinned cortex. Fine granules from chronic GN/nephrosclerosis. Coarse granules from pyelonephritis
enlarged swollen kidney with small yellow-white abscesses, hemorrhagic rim. Caused by ascending infection (most common - E. coli)
Ischemic necrosis of renal papillae - complication of acute pyelonephritis in diabetes/urinary tract obstruction patients

cards.f: Kidney atrophy and compensatory hypertrophy shows
cards.b: one shrunken kidney and one enlarged kidney. Atrophy from atherosclerosis/nephrosclerosis. Hypertrophy from increased workload
Hypertension from renal artery stenosis - atrophic kidney releases renin causing secondary hypertension
enlarged kidney with lobulated/bosselated surface, dilated cystic spaces continuous with pelvis/ureter, pressure atrophy of cortex

cards.f: Difference hydronephrosis vs polycystic kidney disease?
cards.b: Hydronephrosis - dilated calyces continuous with pelvis/ureter (pressure atrophy). Polycystic - separate cysts, no continuity, bilateral
solitary golden-yellow tumour with variegated appearance. Classic triad: gross hematuria, flank pain, palpable abdominal mass. Risk factors: tobacco, VHL disease

cards.f: Characteristic microscopic appearance clear cell RCC?
cards.b: Nests of cells with optically clear cytoplasm (glycogen/lipid washed out), distinct cell borders, thin-walled (chicken-wire) vascular network
soft fish-flesh tumour replacing kidney. Associated with WAGR: Wilm's Tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary abnormalities, Mental Retardation. Microscopy shows triphasic: blastema, epithelium, stroma
Triphasic - blastema (small blue cells), epithelium (tubules/glomeruli), stroma (muscle, cartilage, fat)
exophytic papillary growth - furry towards lumen, solid towards wall. Most common is Transitional Cell Carcinoma. Risk factors: smoking, aniline dyes, schistosomiasis (SCC)
lobulated kidney with yellow-white necrotic areas, excess fat near hilum. Caused by Hepatitis B. Rosary sign is diagnostic feature
onion peel appearance on X-ray. Involves diaphysis of long bones. Genetic translocation: t(11;22)(q24;q12) - EWS-FLI1 fusion
multiple well-circumscribed whitish masses with central umbilication. Most common primary site is stomach

cards.f: Most common benign tumour of liver?
cards.b: Hemangioma
Orphan Annie eye nuclei, nuclear grooves, intranuclear pseudo-inclusions, psammoma bodies. Most common thyroid malignancy
